body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: eba0e477d755c99ac5fbf7d61e6490f76445cfe8 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a second review of a safety-tier change (posted G-code and refusals). It builds on the collaborator review at this head. It does not replace it.

## What looks good

- The cumulative A overtravel refusal names the limit and a remedy. It explains the two-lap plus seam coverage of Rotary Offset. `assets/posts/tormach.cps` (indexFor, the travel test).
- The refusal blocks the post. `aRefuse` raises a warning. The warning count in `posting::post_setup` blocks the file write. The pins in `crates/post/tests/tormach_rotary_travel.rs` also check that the refused +/-361 target never reaches the program.
- The recorded refusal for the B30 tilt now names the tilt, not "simultaneous 4-axis". That is the better diagnostic. The `tormach_fourth_axis` suite pins the indexed law is kept.
- The wrapped-A time law is sound: G93 times the longer of the part-relative path at the programmed feed and the turn at the stated A rate. The bound uses the rounded posted words, not the stream chord. Neither the feed nor the A rate can be passed.
- The G93 mode cannot leak: G94 returns before a plain move, before a turning rapid (head `eba0e477d`), and at each section end.
- Decision records `docs/decisions/2344-rotary-offset-travel.md` and `796-tormach-wrapped-a.md` state the sources, the choices, and the dropped options. The clean-room line holds: the readings are the author's own Hub runs on issue #796, plus public LinuxCNC references.

## Results (built locally on Windows, merged with main)

Trial merge with `origin/main` at `3e47b898b` is clean. Build: `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run` passes. Suites, one by one, all green:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| post/tormach_rotary_travel | 3 passed |
| post/script_tormach | 11 passed |
| post/recorded_streams | 12 passed |
| post/g93_feed | 5 passed |
| post/cycle_hop | 7 passed |
| post/explain_tormach | 3 passed |
| app/tormach_wrapped_a | 12 passed |
| app/tormach_fourth_axis | 12 passed |
| app/fourth_axis_pose | 9 passed |
| app/microarc_test_part | 3 passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes. The wrapped golden comparator passes on Windows here. That covers the platform-rounding case the author could not run.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. The branch carries the four commits of #2342, which is still open with `needs-rework`. This PR supersedes that work in its diff against main. The maintainer should close #2342 as superseded, or merge this PR first. The body says "merge #2342 first"; with this head that order is not needed.
2. `docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md` records the golden comparator with the absolute 0.04 F bound. The final head uses the 0.2 percent relative bound. The amendment stands in the 2344 decision record. A one-line pointer in the 796 file would keep the two aligned.
3. The microARC A rate (360 deg/min) comes from the Hub SIM runs, not a citable vendor page. The decision record says this plainly and calls it conservative. Agreed.

Labels: this PR is a fork PR. Its `merge-ready` label stands, and no label changes with this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
